facts.statement: Redondavenator is a genus of sphenosuchian, which is a type of basal crocodylomorph related to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Redondavenator (meaning "Redonda Formation hunter") is a genus of sphenosuchian, a type of basal crocodylomorph, the clade that comprises the crocodilians and their closest kin.

facts.statement: Redondavenator holds the record for being the largest crocodylomorph known from the Triassic period.
facts.quote: This makes it the largest Triassic crocodylomorph ever recorded.

facts.statement: The minimum estimated skull length of the holotype individual is 60 centimeters.
facts.quote: the minimum estimated skull length for the holotype individual is 60 cm.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2005 by Sterling Nesbitt and his colleagues.
facts.quote: Redondavenator was named in 2005 by Sterling Nesbitt and colleagues.

facts.statement: The type species is named R. quayensis, which refers to Quay County.
facts.quote: The type species is R. quayensis, referring to Quay County.

facts.statement: The fourth and fifth teeth of the upper jaw were enlarged.
facts.quote: The fourth and fifth teeth of the maxilla were enlarged.

facts.statement: The shoulder bones of the animal were robust.
Researchers interpreted the animal as filling a large terrestrial predator role left vacant by the extinction of rauisuchians.
facts.quote: They interpreted it as filling a large terrestrial predator role that had been left empty by the extinction of "rauisuchians".

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Norian stage of the Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of the animal is Crocodylomorpha.

rejected.statement: The animal is known from a partial upper jaw and left shoulder girdle found in the Upper Triassic Redonda Formation in northeastern New Mexico.
rejected.quote: It is known from a partial upper jaw and left shoulder girdle found in rocks of the Norian-Rhaetian-age Upper Triassic Redonda Formation, northeastern New Mexico.
